_note: The [I] tier. Names and record fields that a filter or a neighbour produced and that
nothing has yet checked. Same shape as docs/symbols.json plus two required keys:
basis      what generated it - which filter, which caller, which neighbouring name.
confidence one line saying what would have to be true, and what would refute it.
Nothing here is applied to Ghidra and nothing here may be cited as a finding.
docs/symbols.json is at a deliberately high verified ratio and this file exists so
that bulk work can happen without diluting it. Promotion is one direction only:
run a check that could have failed, then move the entry across and record the check
in its comment. If the check refutes it, delete the entry - do not soften it.
The rate to expect is measured in docs/method.md section 7.3: the subject filter runs
89% correct and the role hypothesis on top of it 58%. So roughly two in five of the
roles below are wrong, and the value of the file is that it says which two in five
are worth checking first rather than that it is right.

functions.name: Merchant_SeasonTick
functions.basis: Position in Season_Advance's call list, between County_RecountMerchants and Army_RecountCountyTroops, and its address - it sits between Merchant_AdvanceAll (0x004280E9) and Merchant_ResetStall (0x0042847C) in the merchant neighbourhood.
functions.confidence: The body is eleven bytes and returns. So the name is a guess at what was removed, and it cannot be checked from this binary at all: an empty function has no evidence in it. Recorded because a reader of Season_Advance needs to know the slot is deliberately empty rather than missing, not because the name is worth anything.
functions.comment: A season pass that does nothing. Called only from Season_Advance.

functions.name: Army_ProcessPendingDisbands
functions.basis: First call in Wages_PayAll, ahead of Army_Starve. Walks every kind-1 unit, calls FUN_004ABA5A on it, and destroys any whose county byte is above 16.
functions.confidence: The stray-army half is directly readable and near-certain; the disband half rests on FUN_004ABA5A, which returns an army's men to its home county's population when unit +0x167 is 1 and clears the flag when it is more - so +0x167 looks like a disband request with a one-season delay, and that reading is unchecked. Cross-subsystem: this belongs to whoever owns armies, not to the season pipeline. Refuted if +0x167 turns out to be set anywhere other than a disband order.
functions.comment: Retires armies at the top of the wage pass: honours pending disbands, then destroys any army standing outside every county.

functions.name: Army_DisbandPending
functions.basis: Sole caller is FUN_004AD39A. Reads unit +0x167: at 1 it adds menTotal back to the home county's population and popArmy and destroys the unit; above 1 it decrements the flag to 0 instead.
functions.confidence: The effect is plain; what is not established is what sets +0x167, and therefore whether this is a disband order, a garrison return, or something else. Find the writer of +0x167 and this either promotes or dies.
functions.comment: Returns an army's men to its home county and destroys it, when unit +0x167 says one is pending.

fields.name: merchantFlag
fields.basis: County_RecountMerchants zeroes it alongside +0x1A4 and +0x1A5, the two merchant fields.
fields.confidence: Zero in every county of every fixture, and nothing else in the corpus writes it, so the zeroing is all the evidence there is. It sits immediately before rationAchieved (+0x15D), so a width error here would be visible; it is a byte. Refuted if a writer turns up outside the merchant code.

fields.name: fieldsOther
fields.basis: County_RecountFields buckets tile graphics 0, 23 and 24 here, next to the three named field tallies.
fields.confidence: Zero in all fourteen counties of the England fixture, so the reproduction that verified the other four tallies could not verify this one - a bucket that never fires is a bucket whose meaning is unknown. Graphic 0 is an empty slot; 23 and 24 are not identified. Needs a save with those tiles.

fields.name: fieldsReclaimable
fields.basis: County_RecountFields buckets tile graphic 25 and above here; Field_SetType switches the reclamation labour share on exactly when it is non-zero.
fields.confidence: The gate in Field_SetType is direct and strong - this counts land the county can reclaim. What is not checked is the graphic band: it is 0 in every fixture, so no save demonstrates which tiles land in it. Promote when a save with wasteland exists.

fields.name: farmStyle
fields.basis: Ai_ManageCountyFarms writes it from g_aiPersonality's farmStyle and immediately dispatches on 0, 1 and 9.
fields.confidence: Strong: the fixture holds only 0, 1 and 9, exactly the dispatched values. Left here rather than promoted because unowned counties also carry 1, and Ai_ManageCountyFarms only writes AI-owned ones, so something at map load writes it too and has not been found. The name may be too narrow.

fields.name: purse
fields.basis: Merchant_Trade credits and debits it instead of realm gold when the realm argument is 0.
fields.confidence: Readable but never exercised: 0 in every fixture, because no unowned county has traded. The claim that an unowned county has a treasury of its own is a real one and it is untested.

fields.name: armyFoodForagers
fields.basis: Ration_Apply adds +0x198 + +0x19C to the county's food requirement when g_optArmiesEat is on, and Panel_Ration draws that same sum against L2.eng 87/8 'men foraging in the county.'. The orphaned ration group 62 has 'Soldiers', 'Foragers', 'take' and 'steal' as four separate strings, which is where the split into two fields comes from.
fields.confidence: That the pair exists and sums into the food bill is certain. Which of the two is soldiers and which is foragers is a guess off the dead string group, and is a coin flip. Both are 0 in every fixture - no fixture has an army standing in a county with Armies Eat on.

fields.name: receivedTotal
fields.basis: Merchant_Trade adds the crown amount to +0x104 and +0x108 on a purchase and to +0x10C and +0x110 on a sale.
fields.confidence: That two accumulators run on spending and two on income is certain. Which of each pair is the season figure and which the running total is not: nothing in the corpus resets either, and all four are 0 in every fixture because no fixture has traded. If neither is ever reset, the pair is something else entirely - two panels rather than two horizons.

globals.name: g_playerSlots
globals.basis: Mp_DropDepartedPlayers tests slot +0x00 for zero; Realm_Eliminate clears +0x00, +0x25, +0x26 and sets +0x27. Stride 0x2C, six entries, one per realm.
globals.confidence: A per-realm table whose first word means 'this realm is still attached' is the only reading that makes both functions work. What the table actually holds - a network peer, a save slot, a controller - is not established, and the name presumes the first.

globals.name: g_playerCount
globals.basis: Decremented by Mp_DropDepartedPlayers each time a realm is dropped.
globals.confidence: One writer, one direction. Nothing here shows what increments it or who reads it.

globals.name: g_tradeGood
globals.basis: Indexes g_merchantStall in the trade panel and selects the branch in the good-to-stock switch.
globals.confidence: Consistent everywhere it appears. Not promoted because the trade screen was not read end to end here - only the transaction underneath it.

globals.name: g_startForcesSetting
globals.basis: Indexes g_startArmoury (stride 0x18) and, alongside g_startTroops's own index, seeds a new game's armoury.
globals.confidence: Both tables have exactly four meaningful rows, so the setting takes four values, which matches a new-game option. Which option, and whether 0..3 runs weakest to strongest, is inferred from the rows being monotonic and nothing else.
